message.content: I don’t have real‑time access to the latest Gini coefficient figures, but the most recent estimates put the United States’ Gini coefficient at roughly **41–42** (using the 2020–2021 data from the U.S. Census Bureau and OECD). This places the U.S. in the mid‑range among high‑income countries, indicating a moderate level of income inequality. If you need the absolute latest figure, you might want to check the latest releases from the U.S. Census Bureau or the World Bank’s World Development Indicators.
